name: Battle of Nicopolis

phases.title: The armies take position
phases.text: The French knights rode out with their backs to Nicopolis. The Hungarians, Hospitallers and Germans stayed behind them, while the Turks stood on the slope to the south with their reserve of sipahis out of sight on the plateau.

phases.title: The French charge the Turkish front line
phases.text: The French knights charged and crushed the untrained conscripts at the front of the Turkish army. The conscripts broke and the knights pressed on towards the trained infantry behind them.

phases.title: The knights fight through the stakes
phases.text: The knights came under heavy fire from archers and were held up by rows of sharpened stakes. Many were unhorsed or dismounted to pull the stakes up, and the Turkish infantry fled behind the sipahis.

phases.title: The knights press up the slope on foot
phases.text: The younger knights overruled Coucy and Vienne, who wanted a pause to reform, and insisted on pursuit. The French went on up the hill, more than half of them on foot, while sipahis appear to have swept down along the flanks.

phases.title: The knights reach the plateau and meet the sipahis
phases.text: Struggling in heavy armour, the French reached the plateau at the top of the slope, where they had expected to find fleeing Turks. They found instead a fresh corps of sipahis that Bayezid had kept in reserve.

phases.title: The sipahis counter-attack on the plateau
phases.text: The sipahis surged forward, sounding trumpets, banging kettle drums and shouting the Tekbir. Some French knights fled back down the slope, and the rest fought on.

phases.title: Nevers is taken and the French yield
phases.text: The Turks threatened to overwhelm Nevers, and his bodyguard threw themselves to the ground to plead for his life. The Turks took Nevers prisoner, and seeing this, the rest of the French yielded.

phases.title: The Transylvanians and Wallachians leave the field
phases.text: The Hungarians and other nationalities were in confused combat on the plain. At the sight of a stampede of riderless horses, the Transylvanians and Wallachians decided the day was lost and abandoned the field.

phases.title: Sigismund resists the envelopment
phases.text: Sigismund, the Master of Rhodes and the Germans fought to prevent the sipahis from enveloping them, and both sides suffered heavy losses.

phases.title: The Serbian knights join the Turks
phases.text: The Turks received a reinforcement of 1,500 Serbian knights under Stefan Lazarević, which proved critical to the outcome of the fight.

phases.title: Sigismund's force is overwhelmed
phases.text: Sigismund's force was overwhelmed. Sigismund and the Master escaped on a fisherman's boat, and the rest of his army, after a deal was made, surrendered.

note: The accounts are in conflict and no coherent account of the movements can be had, so the plan shows one reading of them. The Transylvanians and Wallachians are placed on the allied side, since the accounts do not say where they stood. The sipahis on the flanks may be the same troops as the reserve on the plateau; the accounts do not say, so they are drawn as a separate force. The French mounted archers rode with the knights and are not drawn apart. The Turkish flight and the exact line of the slope are not given.
